title: BananaMind 2 Pro: We've (almost) matched SmolLM2 at 20x fewer tokens... Trained On a 5070 Ti
gist: A community developer trained BananaMind 2 Pro, a ~140M-parameter language model, on just 100B tokens on a single consumer RTX 5070 Ti GPU, retaining 96% of SmolLM2-135M's benchmark score with 20x fewer tokens and beating it in human-preference voting, while trailing badly on code generation and arguing training-token count alone doesn't determine small-model quality.

insights.claim: The author's central takeaway is that training-token count alone does not determine how good a small language model will be; architecture, data quality, data mixture, optimization, tokenizer choices, and training strategy all matter as much or more.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Reframes small-model training investment away from simply maximizing token count toward data curation and architecture choices, relevant to anyone evaluating small-model training economics or claims of efficiency.
insights.quote: training-token count alone doesn't determine how good a small language model will be
insights.locator: What I'm taking away from this

insights.claim: BananaMind 2 Pro, a roughly 140M-parameter model trained on just 100B tokens, retained 96.08% of SmolLM2-135M's average benchmark score across a nine-benchmark suite despite using 20 times fewer training tokens than SmolLM2's 2 trillion-token training run.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: A strong self-reported data point for diminishing returns on token scaling at small model sizes, though it comes from a single unverified community project rather than an independent evaluation.
insights.quote: Across all these benchmarks, BananaMind 2 Pro has retained 96.08% of SmolLM2-135M's benchmark score while using 20× fewer training tokens.

insights.claim: Despite using six times fewer tokens than SmolLM-135M's original 600B-token training run, BananaMind 2 Pro outperforms it on HellaSwag, ArithMark 3, ArithMark 2, and Base Bench.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Suggests a newer, education-and-synthetic-data-heavy training recipe can beat an older, more token-heavy training run on several tasks, reinforcing that data quality can substitute for raw token volume.

insights.claim: While BananaMind 2 Pro trails SmolLM2-135M on most static academic benchmarks, it ranks #1 with 1163.8 Elo on the community SLM Arena human-preference leaderboard versus SmolLM2-135M's #6 ranking at 1082.1 Elo, an 81.7 Elo lead, though this is based on only 51 and 43 total battles respectively.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Standard academic benchmarks may not track human-perceived output quality even directionally for small models, though the very small battle counts here mean this specific ranking shouldn't be overweighted.
insights.quote: That's an 81 Elo lead for BananaMind 2 Pro.
insights.locator: But benchmarks aren't the whole story

themes.theme: Code generation remains the weak spot

insights.claim: Code generation is BananaMind 2 Pro's clearest weakness: it trails SmolLM2-135M by 78 points and the original SmolLM-135M by 178 points on the Code benchmark, a gap the author attributes to needing further work rather than to token count alone.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Domain-specific capability like code appears to track the proportion of domain-specific training data (only 2.31% of the mix was Python-focused) even within an otherwise token-efficient recipe, meaning per-capability data allocation matters, not just aggregate efficiency.
insights.quote: BananaMind 2 Pro trails SmolLM2 by 78 points and SmolLM by 178 points.
insights.locator: Code still has room to improve

insights.claim: The entire 100B-token BananaMind 2 Pro training run was completed on a single consumer RTX 5070 Ti 16GB GPU rather than a datacenter accelerator like an H100 or A100, which the author frames as central to a thesis that meaningful language-model training shouldn't require massive GPU clusters.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence for the compute-democratization narrative in small-model research, indicating sub-200M-parameter LM training and experimentation is increasingly accessible without cluster-scale compute.
insights.quote: meaningful language-model training and experimentation shouldn't be limited to people with access to massive GPU clusters
insights.locator: And yes, it was trained on a 5070 TI

insights.claim: BananaMind 2 Pro's 100B-token training mixture was roughly 76% general web and educational data (FineWeb-Edu at 50.17% plus DCLM at 26.13%) and roughly 24% specialized synthetic, math, and code data (Cosmopedia-v2, FineMath-4+, and NPSet-2 Python Edu).
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Provides a concrete, replicable reference data-mixture recipe for token-efficient small-model training that other small-model developers could benchmark against.

insights.claim: The author states the next round of BananaMind improvements will come from completely new architectures rather than further scaling the same token-efficiency recipe, suggesting the current approach is seen as reaching diminishing returns.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Watch whether the next BananaMind release changes architecture rather than just scale, a signal of what limitation the team believes it has hit with the current recipe.
insights.quote: Our next improvements will be completly new architectures.

insights.claim: The author disclosed using an AI assistant heavily to write the blog post itself, asking it to edit only one specific sentence about the RTX 5070 Ti, but the assistant rewrote much of the surrounding text without the author noticing, which several commenters flagged as reading like generic AI-generated writing.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Illustrates a real failure mode of AI editing assistants (unintended scope creep) and a broader authenticity concern for AI/ML community blog content, even when the author openly discloses it after being called out.
insights.quote: So I wrote it and told it to change only this part: And yes, it was trained on a 5070 TIAnd didnt realize it changed everything else.
insights.locator: Banaxi-Tech Article author about 4 hours ago

insights.claim: The original benchmark comparison chart incorrectly stated SmolLM was trained on 200B tokens; a community commenter corrected this to the actual figure of 600B tokens, and the author acknowledged the error and fixed it after publication.
insights.speaker: Banaxi
insights.so_what: Shows self-published community AI benchmarking comparisons go through informal, post-hoc community fact-checking rather than pre-publication review, a data-quality caution when citing such comparisons.
insights.quote: Smollm-135m was trained on 600b tokens, not 200b
